as_told.title: Grusch's documents to IC Inspector General Monheim

plain: A former intelligence officer turned whistleblower named David Grusch is said to have handed hundreds of pages of documents to the Intelligence Community Inspector General, or ICIG, the watchdog that takes complaints from inside the US spy agencies. Grusch filed the complaint in 2022. Michels tells this again and again on the show, in his own words. In his account the pages describe a secret, decades-old programme to recover crashed UFOs, which the subject calls a legacy crash retrieval programme. He says the inspector general, Thomas Monheim, called the claims "urgent and credible". The count changes between tellings. Most of the time Michels says hundreds of pages, once he says "presumably" hundreds, and once he says "over a thousand pages". In another telling he passes the story on from someone he names only as Omar. A UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells it separately: he thinks it may be "a thousand pages plus", and says Monheim is "now out" of the job and nothing has been done with them. If true, the government's own watchdog would have taken claims of hidden crash recoveries seriously.
